The Aardwolf (Proteles cristatus) is a small, insectivorous hyaenid found across the savannas and grasslands of eastern and southern Africa, feeding almost exclusively on harvester termites. Under a stable core body temperature of 39 °C [T = 39 °C], the gestation period lasts approximately 84 days [tg = approximately 84 days], a duration consistent with other small-bodied hyaenids. Newborn pups weigh approximately 275 grams [Wwb = approximately 275 grams] at birth, a moderate neonatal mass reflecting a degree of altriciality typical of burrow-reared carnivoran young.

Juvenile Aardwolves remain within the natal den for an extended period, nursing on rich milk before transitioning to independent foraging on termites. At the same thermal regime of 39 °C [T = 39 °C], weaning is completed at approximately 90 days after birth [tx = approximately 90 days after birth], after which pups begin accompanying the mother on nocturnal foraging bouts to learn termite-detection skills essential for survival. This gradual transition to independent foraging reflects the specialized dietary skills required to locate and consume termite colonies efficiently.

Sexual maturation is considerably delayed, with puberty in females attained at approximately 1.75 years after birth [tp = approximately 1.75 years after birth] under the same thermal conditions at a temperature of 39 °C [T = 39 °C]. This protracted juvenile period allows young Aardwolves to establish their own foraging territories and refine the specialized behaviors needed to exploit a diet that is highly seasonal and patchily distributed across the savanna. Reproductive output is modest, with a maximum of approximately 2.5 pups produced per litter each year [Ri = of approximately 2.5 pups produced per litter each year] at the same reference temperature. Longevity in the Aardwolf reaches a maximum of approximately 20 years [am = approximately 20 years] at 39 °C [T = 39 °C], a considerable lifespan for a small hyaenid and one that supports repeated annual breeding attempts across a long reproductive lifetime.
